propositions: Gerrit Verify currently runs thousands of real Pandoc subprocess conversions over the complete DC wiki corpus, consuming 184+ seconds on the macOS critical path during corpus phases.
ADR 0095 mandates real Pandoc binary for every conversion assertion, creating a testing-boundary constraint that prevents moving expensive full-corpus replay out of the hot path.

The approved design relocates complete real-Pandoc corpus replay from Gerrit Verify to a dedicated weekly/manual job in external-integration.yml with ubuntu-latest and macos-latest matrix coverage, while preserving three representative live corpus bodies and all assertion classes against committed outputs in Gerrit Verify.

ADR 0096 must narrowly supersede only the every-conversion-assertion-live clause of ADR 0095, preserving all production renderer invariants, pin/provenance probes, platform boundaries, and safety assertions.
The external-integration workflow is currently Ubuntu-only and requires implementation to add explicit macOS runner support for the pandoc-corpus-replay job.
Implementation must obtain paired A/B performance evidence and ensure version drift and platform-specific binary fingerprints fail fast with deterministic fixture regeneration.
